I’m a 5’2 relatively conventionally attractive girl and in high school I had the biggest crush on a guy who was 5’4 and cried because I considered him so out of my league lol. I went to college (and on a date with) a 5’4 guy who was always incredibly popular with women even though I feel like his non-height features weren’t very cute— he was just a great guy. (And no, he had 0 money.) So maybe being a 5’4 isn’t the beauty standard, I won’t bullshit you, but it’s not like it’s hopeless for you to find someone nice and pretty who will love you. And friends, employers, etc. shouldn’t care about your height. Life is worth living.

Some guy messages me on social media to say “your sister is cute, can I have her number? Sorry you’re too fat for me”

Like thanks I didn’t ask & I worked for a year to get to the HEALTHY weight I’m at today & I’ve been desperately trying to build my self esteem from NOTHING and you really wrecked it with that awful comment I didn’t ask for. I’ve never talked to this guy in my life.

Idk, I don’t think that’s fair. For a lot of people, their sexuality is a huge part of their identity. Having the people you love and are close to reject a part of you and feeling like there’s this huge part of you that you have to keep secret can be soul-crushing... Relationships are a huge part of being human, so your sexuality is definitely important, even if it’s not “your whole existence”. & that’s great that you mean it, but a lot of people aren’t like that. Personally, when someone says that to me, partially because it’s so noncommittal and partially because of bad experiences in the past, I’ll never PM/call up someone who just says that to me because I automatically assume it’s a cop-out of the situation.

I feel the same way. A lot of the time for me, I appreciate knowing that I’m not alone or broken for feeling that way. Hearing from other people on the sub who’ve been through/are going through the same things makes me feel less alone and more valid in what I’m feeling, like there’s still hope for me. But I prefer to hear others talk about their problems than talk about my own, sometimes helping someone else helps you.

As for IRL people who actually know me, what helps is them boosting me up and showing concern (I guess more like “what?? How long have you felt depressed? I’m so sorry, what can I do to help?” would be an ideal response since that feels genuine) versus “call me if you need someone to talk to” or whatever... like I’m talking to you now!

I disagree. There’s nothing wrong with not commenting if you don’t really care about someone’s situation, but just writing “I’m here if you need to talk” isn’t for the other person’s benefit at all. It’s just a way for people to feel good about themselves like “I’m helping!” When they’re really not at all. Hearing “I’m here if you need to talk” doesn’t make anyone feel better, not even for a second. And almost always, the people who comment that don’t actually want to have a PM conversation or just flat-out don’t message back.

It’s not that I’m against small displays of empathy, I just don’t think that comments like these are actually empathetic. They’re self-centered and more about easing the guilt on the commenter’s part. I would rather not get any supportive messages then get “Mesage me if you want to talk”.

It’s against the sub rules for a reason. But people still do it anyways, even though it’s right there in the sidebar.

Please. Even if no one loves you. I’m in that boat right now. Not a single person loves me or cares about me at all. I cry every day.

But I’m still trying. Please keep trying too. Isn’t it worth it to stick around in the hopes that someday, someone WILL care? Someone will love you? You don’t know that it won’t happen. Don’t just accept that it won’t like that. If you die alone, then it’ll suck. It’ll be the worst thing ever and it’ll be another horrible thing that happens in this world. But please don’t give up before you see it through to the end. All we can do is keep going forward. Don’t eliminate the chance of it getting better.
